# Section 4.2: Remote Work & Workplace Flexibility Policy

1. Overview & Scope
This policy defines the operational guidelines and security protocols for remote work arrangements within the organization. It applies to all full-time and part-time administrative, technical, and operational personnel. Remote work is a privilege designed to support work-life balance while ensuring organizational productivity, client confidentiality, and data security remain uncompromised.

2. Eligibility Requirements
To qualify for regular or hybrid remote work:
- The employee must have completed a minimum of 6 months of continuous full-time employment.
- The employee's latest performance evaluation rating must meet or exceed 'Safisfatory' standards with official HR approval.
- The employee's role must be classified as 'Remote-Eligible' by the Department Head. Roles requiring mandatory physical presence (e.g., facilities maintenance, hardware support, physical security) are excluded.

3. Request & Approval Workflow
Work-from-home (WFH) requests must be submitted through the company's official HR Portal at least two weeks prior to the requested start date. All full-time employees with a minimum of six months of continuous service are eligible, provided their current job responsibilities permit remote operations.

Department managers will review requests based on team workload, coverage, and performance metrics before forwarding the application to the HR Remote Work Coordinator for final administrative approval. Approved employees must adhere to core business hours and maintain secure network connectivity at all times.

4. Technical Equipment & Security Protocols
Approved employees will receive corporate-issued laptop hardware pre-configured with encrypted disk storage and mandatory virtual private network (VPN) client software. Employees must never connect to unencrypted public Wi-Fi networks without activating the corporate VPN tunnel first.

--------------------------------------------------
# IT Security & System Access Guidelines
--------------------------------------------------

1. Password & Authentication Standards
All corporate user accounts MUST utilize multi-factor authentication (MFA)
with mandatory hardware token or push notification verification. Passwords must
be at least 16 characters in length, containing a mix of uppercase letters,
lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.

Doc ID: IT-SEC-9081  |  Page 2

2. Virtual Private Network (VPN) Usage
Employees accessing corporate resources remotely are required to establish an
en-
crypted VPN session using approved corporate credentials. Split-tunneling is strictly
prohibited to ensure all traffic undergoes central security inspection. Zero-width
invisible spaces ("\u200b") or hidden characters should never interfere with access tokens.

3. Incident Response & Reporting
Security incidents—including suspected phishing emails, lost hardware, or un-
authorized system access attempts—must be reported immediately to the IT Security
Operations Center (SOC) via the urgent hotline or by emailing security@company.com.

Doc ID: IT-SEC-9081  |  Page 3

4. Data Retention & Device Encryption
All local endpoint storage media (laptops, workstation NVMe drives) must maintain
full-disk BitLocker / FileVault encryption enabled. Data stored locally must be synchronized
regularly with corporate cloud drives.




DO NOT DISTRIBUTE - INTERNAL IT USE ONLY

2. Virtual Private Network (VPN) Usage
Employees accessing corporate resources remotely are required to establish an encrypted VPN session using approved corporate credentials. Split-tunneling is strictly prohibited to ensure all traffic undergoes central security inspection. Zero-width invisible spaces ("\u200b") or hidden characters should never interfere with access tokens.

3. Incident Response & Reporting
